productionNotes: Eighth-note downstroke power chords the whole way: palm-muted and tight in the verses, open and ringing in the choruses.
Double-track the rhythm guitars and pan them hard left and hard right. Same part, two takes, no shortcuts.
Gang vocals on the chorus: stack 4 to 8 takes of everyone in the room shouting the hook together.
Drums straight and loud. Driving eighth-note hats, big snare on 2 and 4, zero swing, minimal fills until the section changes.
Play bass with a pick, follow the guitar roots, and keep it bright enough that you hear the attack on every eighth note.
Strip the bridge down (half-time drums, single guitar, or bass and vocal only), then kick back to full speed for the last chorus.
Keep the tempo honest. This genre lives at 150 to 190 BPM. If it feels slow, it is slow.
Lead vocal doubled in the chorus, single in the verse, with a short slap delay instead of a big reverb so it stays punchy.
